questions.stem: Nitrobenzene is reduced with tin and hydrochloric acid, followed by treatment with NaOH. The product is
questions.explanation: Sn/HCl is a strong reducing system that reduces the nitro group completely to the amino group. The product forms as the anilinium salt, and NaOH liberates the free amine, aniline. Reduction in a neutral or alkaline medium can stop at intermediate products such as azobenzene.

optionRationale.1: Benzamide has a C=O group and cannot form from nitrobenzene by reduction.
optionRationale.4: Azobenzene is formed from nitrobenzene by reduction in alkaline medium, not with Sn/HCl.

questions.objective: Recall reduction of nitro compounds to amines

questions.stem: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines, is
questions.explanation: Benzenesulfonyl chloride, C$_6$H$_5$SO$_2$Cl, reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulphonamides and does not react with tertiary amines. The solubility of the sulphonamide in alkali then distinguishes the classes.

optionRationale.1: Benzoyl chloride is used in benzoylation, not in the Hinsberg test.
optionRationale.2: Benzenediazonium chloride is used in coupling and substitution reactions.
optionRationale.4: Phthalic anhydride is used in the Gabriel synthesis through phthalimide.

questions.stem: Bromomethane is treated with KCN to give X. X is reduced with H$_2$/Ni to give Y. Y is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$Br + KCN gives CH$_3$CN (X). Catalytic hydrogenation of the nitrile gives CH$_3$CH$_2$NH$_2$ (Y), ethanamine. This sequence ascends the amine series by one carbon atom, in contrast to the Hofmann bromamide reaction, which descends it by one carbon atom.

optionRationale.1: Methanamine has one carbon, fewer than the nitrile; it would result from the Hofmann bromamide reaction.
optionRationale.2: Ethanamide is a hydrolysis product of the nitrile, not a reduction product.
optionRationale.3: Propan-1-amine would need a three-carbon nitrile.

questions.stem: Aniline is treated with excess bromine water. The product is
questions.explanation: The -NH$_2$ group strongly activates the ring towards electrophilic substitution at the ortho and para positions. In bromine water all three positions are brominated, so a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline forms.

optionRationale.2: 4-Bromoaniline would form only if the activation were reduced first, for example by acetylation.
optionRationale.3: 2-Bromoaniline would form only if the activation were reduced first, for example by acetylation.
optionRationale.4: The -NH$_2$ group directs to ortho and para, not meta.

questions.stem: Fluorobenzene can be prepared from benzenediazonium chloride by treating it with
options: fluoroboric acid (HBF$_4$) and then heating the product
questions.explanation: In the Balz-Schiemann reaction benzenediazonium chloride reacts with HBF$_4$ to give benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate, which precipitates. Heating this dry salt then gives fluorobenzene, BF$_3$ and nitrogen gas. Fluorides cannot be made by the Sandmeyer route.

optionRationale.3: CuCl in HCl gives chlorobenzene by the Sandmeyer reaction.
optionRationale.4: H$_3$PO$_2$ replaces the diazonium group by hydrogen to give benzene.

questions.stem: The base dissociation constant of methylamine is $K_b = 4.4\times10^{-4}$ at 298 K. What is the pH of a 0.10 M aqueous solution of methylamine?
questions.explanation: For a weak base $[\mathrm{OH^-}] \approx \sqrt{K_b C} = \sqrt{4.4\times10^{-4} \times 0.10} = 6.6\times10^{-3}$ M. Then pOH $= 2.18$ and pH $= 14 - 2.18 \approx 11.8$. Solving the quadratic exactly gives nearly the same value.

optionRationale.1: This treats the base as fully ionised, which would give [OH$^-$] = 0.10 M.
optionRationale.2: This is the pOH, not the pH.
optionRationale.4: This is the pK$_b$ of methylamine, not the pH.

questions.objective: Calculate the pH of a weak amine solution

questions.stem: A compound X (C$_3$H$_9$N) reacts with benzenesulfonyl chloride to give a product that is insoluble in aqueous KOH. X also gives a yellow oily liquid with nitrous acid. X is
questions.explanation: A sulphonamide that is insoluble in alkali means that the nitrogen has no hydrogen left, so X is a secondary amine. Secondary amines give yellow oily N-nitrosoamines with HNO$_2$. The secondary amine with formula C$_3$H$_9$N is N-methylethanamine.

optionRationale.1: Propan-1-amine is primary and gives a sulphonamide that dissolves in KOH.
optionRationale.2: Propan-2-amine is primary and gives a sulphonamide that dissolves in KOH.
optionRationale.3: A tertiary amine does not react with benzenesulfonyl chloride.

questions.objective: Identify an amine from Hinsberg and nitrous acid tests

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Aniline is a weaker base than cyclohexylamine.
Reason (R): Aniline dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In aniline the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the ring and is less available for protonation, so it is a weaker base than cyclohexylamine. Aniline does dissolve in dilute HCl by forming a soluble salt, but this is true of any amine and does not explain its relative basicity.

optionRationale.1: The reason does not explain the relative basicity, so it is not the correct explanation.
optionRationale.3: The assertion is true: aniline is the weaker base.
optionRationale.4: The reason is true: aniline forms anilinium chloride with HCl.

questions.objective: Explain the basicity of aryl and alkyl amines

questions.stem: Match the method in List-I with the feature in List-II.
questions.explanation: In the Hofmann bromamide reaction the amine formed has one carbon less than the amide (A-II). The Gabriel synthesis gives only pure aliphatic primary amines (B-III). A nitro compound is reduced with Sn/HCl or by catalytic hydrogenation (C-IV). Ammonolysis of alkyl halides gives a mixture of amines and a quaternary salt (D-I).

optionRationale.2: This code interchanges the matches of A and B; the correct pairs are A-II and B-III.
optionRationale.3: This code interchanges the matches of C and D; the correct pairs are C-IV and D-I.
optionRationale.4: This code interchanges the matches of A and C; the correct pairs are A-II and C-IV.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about aniline.
A. Aniline is a weaker base than ethylamine.
B. Aniline turns brown on standing in air.
C. Acetylation of aniline reduces the activating effect of the -NH$_2$ group.
D. Direct nitration of aniline gives only the para isomer.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Aniline is weaker than ethylamine because the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the ring, it darkens in air by oxidation, and acetylation turns the -NH$_2$ group into an amide that donates less strongly. Direct nitration gives a mixture of ortho, meta and para products, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is wrong because nitration gives a mixture, and C is also correct.
optionRationale.3: D is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.4: It includes the wrong statement D and omits the correct statements A and C.

questions.objective: Recall properties and reactions of aniline
